samples:
If a friend asks whether you like a haircut you think looks bad, what should you say?
other / Change the subject or give a vague answer / Say you love it / Say it's not your favorite but mention something that works / Tell them plainly you don't like it

When is keeping a secret for a friend no longer right?
A promised secret should always be kept / other / When it involves a crime / Whenever keeping it makes you uncomfortable / When someone could be seriously harmed / When it hurts another person you care about

Should you trust a stranger by default, or should trust be earned?
Trust has to be earned over time / Assume good faith until shown otherwise / Trust small things by default, big things only when earned

Which is worse: a lie told to gain an advantage, or a lie told to avoid punishment?
equally_bad / gain_advantage / avoid_punishment

Which kind of dishonesty bothers you most?
Leaving out important facts / Inflating the truth / Insincere praise / Stating things known to be false / Saying you'll do something and not doing it

Is it more important to keep a promise or to do what turns out best when circumstances change?
do_what_is_best / keep_the_promise / depends_on_the_promise

When a surprise party requires lying to the guest of honor, is that kind of lie acceptable?
No, it's still lying / Completely fine / Better to be evasive than to lie outright / Fine, but lie as little as possible

If you could read your partner's messages without them ever knowing, would checking be a breach of trust?
no / yes_always / only_without_good_reason

Should you tell someone about a mistake of yours that they will never discover?
No, it would only cause pain / Yes, always / Only if it affects them

What should you do if a close friend asks you to lie to their boss to cover for them?
Refuse / Cover for them this once / Avoid lying but don't volunteer information / Cover for them whenever asked

Which is a bigger betrayal of trust?
Repeating something told in confidence / Breaking an important promise / Lying directly when asked

Is cheating in a casual board game with friends a real breach of honesty?
No, it's part of the fun / Yes, cheating is cheating / Only a minor one

child.label: Honesty Dilemmas
child.description: Questions about what the answerer thinks is right in specific dilemmas about lying, white lies, painful truths, keeping promises, and rebuilding trust.
child.not_for: Ratings of how many people would agree with a rule of thumb about honesty or trust (use Honesty Rules of Thumb).
examples: Is it okay to lie about liking a gift?
Should you keep a promise to someone who has died?
